questions.optionB: Putting thoughts into a communicable form

questions.optionC: Using technical language, the listener doesn't understand

Which is a strength of written communication?

questions.optionA: Using only one type of communication

questions.en: Your friend is telling you about a problem they're having with another friend. Which response shows the best active listening?
questions.optionA: "Oh, that is just drama. You need to get over it."
questions.optionB: "Have you tried just ignoring them? That's what I would do."
questions.optionC: "I know exactly how you feel. Let me tell you about what happened to me..."
questions.optionD: "Wow, that sounds tough. So, you are saying you feel left out because..."

questions.en: Which sentence is the clearest and most concise?
questions.optionA: "Because it is raining, we should postpone the picnic."
questions.optionB: "Well, you know, like, the weather, it is, I'm, not really, you know, picnic-y, so..."
questions.optionC: "Due to the fact that it is raining outside right now, I am of the opinion that we should probably postpone the picnic that we had previously planned for today."
questions.optionD: "Considering the current meteorological conditions, the outdoor recreational activity will have to be rescheduled."

questions.en: You are talking to a classmate who just moved here from another country and doesn't speak much Urdu. What's the best thing to do?
questions.optionA: Talk loudly so they can understand you better.
questions.optionB: Use lots of big words to help them learn English faster.
questions.optionC: Speak slowly and clearly, using simple words and maybe some pictures.
questions.optionD: Just talk to your other friends and ignore them until they learn English.

questions.en: What would most likely cause a communication problem?
questions.optionA: Listening carefully to what someone says.
questions.optionD: Trying to understand how someone else is feeling.

questions.en: Your friend is upset because he didn't become the part of the basketball team. What's the most empathetic thing to say?
questions.optionA: "Do not worry, you can try out next year."
questions.optionB: "I understand you are disappointed. That must be frustrating."
questions.optionC: "It is no big deal. There are other teams you can join."
questions.optionD: "Just forget about it. It is not worth getting upset over."
